abstract: This review examines empirical evidence on AI's impact on productivity and labor markets, finding that labor market pressure from AI exposure concentrates in entry-level positions within occupations most affected by AI technology, with workforce adjustment occurring through task reallocation rather than broad displacement.
keyFindings: AI-related labor market pressure is concentrated in entry-level segments of highly exposed occupations rather than distributed across skill levels
Adjustment to AI adoption is occurring at the margin through task reallocation within existing positions
methodology: Review of empirical evidence on AI's productivity and labor market effects; specific data sources, sample details, and analytical methods not specified in excerpt.
